name: Box Jump
doThisNotThat: Jump high and land soft and quiet on a box at hip height or lower. Don't pick a box so tall that you land in a deep tuck: that just tests hip flexibility.
steps: Stand a half-step from the box, feet hip-width, tripod feet screwed into the floor.
Load fast: arms swing back while hips hinge to about 1/4 squat.
Drive the floor away and swing the arms up hard, hips then knees then ankles.
Land with the whole foot at the same time, knees over toes, in an athletic quarter squat, and freeze 1 s.
Step down, never jump down; reset fully before the next rep.
cues: Push the floor through the ceiling
Land like a cat: silent box
homeSwap: Jump onto the bottom stair or a sturdy step, or do max-height squat jumps with a stuck landing on the floor.
note: Flat feet show up on the landing: watch for knees caving in. If they do, lower the box and own Step-and-Stick landings before chasing height.

name: Seated Box Jump
doThisNotThat: Start fully still on a bench so no stretch-reflex helps you. That isolates pure concentric rate of force, so don't rock forward first.
steps: Sit on a bench at knee height, feet flat under the knees, a box 1-2 ft in front.
Lean the chest slightly forward, arms back.
Explode up and forward with an arm swing and land on the box in a quarter squat.
Stick it 1 s, step down, sit fully back down before the next rep.
homeSwap: Sit on a chair or bed edge and jump to a max-height floor landing; stick it.
note: Your weak spot is getting going from a dead stop (late reactions). Starting from zero trains the first 100 ms of force, which is exactly where you are slow.

name: Broad Jump
doThisNotThat: Jump out at about a 45° takeoff and stick the landing. Don't fall forward or step after: a jump only counts if you land balanced.
steps: Toes behind a line, feet hip-width, tripod feet.
Arms swing back as the hips hinge fast to a quarter squat.
Throw the arms forward and up, extending hips, knees and ankles together at about 45°.
Pull the knees through and land heels-to-mid-foot in a half squat, arms forward.
Hold 2 s, measure from the line to the back heel.
cues: Throw your hips to the far wall
homeSwap: Same drill; mark distance with a sock or tape on the floor.
note: This is your weekly athleticism test. Same warm-up, best of 3; the number climbing is the visible win.

name: Depth Jump
doThisNotThat: Step off a low box (12-18 in) and leave the floor as fast as possible. Don't drop from a high box and sink into a deep squat: that's a slow jump, not a reactive one.
steps: Stand on a 12-18 in box, toes at the edge.
Step off, don't hop down.
Hit the floor on the balls of the feet with stiff ankles and rebound up instantly, under ~0.25 s.
Reach and jump max height, then land quietly in a quarter squat.
homeSwap: Step off the bottom stair (about 7-8 in) into a rebound jump, or do pogo-into-max jump.
note: Advanced: earn it with 4+ weeks of pogos and clean box jumps first. Low volume (3x3-4), because reactive work is about contact quality.

name: Drop Jump
doThisNotThat: Step off a low box and either stick a silent landing or rebound fast with a short contact. Don't let the knees cave or the heels slam.
steps: Stand on a 12 in box.
Step off with one foot and land on two feet together.
Land in an athletic quarter squat with knees over toes and freeze 2 s (stick version), or rebound instantly (reactive version).
Reset fully.
cues: Knees push out over the pinky toes
homeSwap: Step off the bottom stair into a stuck landing.
note: Drop landings teach the brain that landing is safe, which loosens the threat-state grip. Start with the stick version before going reactive.

name: Pogo Hops
doThisNotThat: Short, stiff, quiet bounces off the balls of the feet with locked knees. Don't do mini squat jumps.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width, weight on the balls of the feet.
Knees soft but almost locked; ankles do the work.
Bounce fast off the floor, heels barely kissing it.
Arms swing small and quick in rhythm.
note: Do 2x10-20 before every run: it tunes the Achilles spring that XC economy depends on, and preps the feet that flatten when you are tired.

name: Ankle Hops
doThisNotThat: Hop forward in small, fast contacts using only the ankles. Don't bend the knees to make up for a lazy ankle.
steps: Stand tall, arms bent like running.
Hop forward 6-12 in per contact using only the ankles.
Land and leave on the balls of the feet with the toes pulled up just before contact.
Go 10-15 m, walk back.
homeSwap: Hop in place or down a hallway.
note: Pulling the toes up before contact pre-stiffens the arch, which matters more for you with flat feet.

name: Tuck Jump
doThisNotThat: Jump straight up and bring the knees to the hands at the top, then land soft and centered. Don't pike, kick the heels back, or land with the knees in.
steps: Feet hip-width, hands out at chest height, palms down.
Dip fast and jump vertically.
Drive the knees up to touch the hands at peak.
Extend the legs back down and land quietly in the same spot.
homeSwap: Same drill; do it on carpet or grass.
note: A tuck jump is also a landing test: if your knees cave on landing, cut reps and fix it with drop landings.

name: Squat Jump
doThisNotThat: Pause 2 s at the bottom, then explode. With no bounce you train pure concentric power. Don't do fast sloppy reps for a burn.
steps: Feet shoulder-width, tripod feet, hands on hips or behind the head.
Sit to a half squat and hold 2 s.
Explode straight up as high as possible.
Land soft and reset completely between reps.
homeSwap: Same drill; hold light dumbbells at your sides only if height stays the same.
note: Stop the set when the height visibly drops. Pareja-Blanco 2017 showed that stopping early keeps the speed gains.

name: Countermovement Jump
doThisNotThat: A fast dip into a full-out vertical with an arm swing. Don't do a slow, deep dip.
steps: Stand tall under a wall or a reach target.
Swing the arms back as you drop fast to about a quarter squat.
Reverse instantly: arms up, hips, knees and ankles extend.
Reach high, land soft.
homeSwap: Same; use a wall and chalk or a sticky note to mark the reach.
note: This is your weekly vertical test. The arm swing adds a lot of height, so always test it the same way.

name: Split Jump
doThisNotThat: Jump vertically out of a split stance and switch legs in the air, landing balanced. Don't bounce through sloppy lunges for reps.
steps: Split stance, front shin vertical, back knee 2 in off the floor.
Explode up, switch legs mid-air.
Land in the mirrored split with the front foot flat and knee over the toes.
Reset 1 s, repeat.
cues: Land with the front foot glued
note: Front-knee collapse on landing is the flat-foot cascade in action. Screw the front foot into the floor on every landing.

name: Lateral Bound
doThisNotThat: Push off one leg sideways for distance and stick the landing on the other leg for 1-2 s. Don't bounce through for speed before you can stick it.
steps: Stand on the right leg, slight hinge.
Load the hip, then drive the floor away sideways.
Land on the left leg with the knee over the pinky toe, hip back, and freeze.
Bound back.
note: This builds the side-to-side push for tennis, pickleball, basketball defense and cutting. The stick trains the outer hip to stop your knee caving.

name: Skater Bound
doThisNotThat: Bound diagonally forward-side with a quick landing and rhythm. Don't go straight sideways with a heavy, flat-footed landing.
steps: Start on one leg.
Push off diagonally forward and to the side.
Land on the other foot, balls first, then whole foot, with the hip loaded.
Rebound into the next bound with a smooth rhythm.
note: Do the stick version (Lateral Bound) first for 2-3 weeks, then move to rhythm skaters.

name: Single-Leg Hop
doThisNotThat: Hop forward on one leg and stick each landing. Don't chain hops before you can land each one balanced.
steps: Stand on one leg, tripod foot.
Hop forward 1-3 ft.
Land on the same leg, knee over the second toe, and hold 2 s.
Progress to continuous hops later.
cues: Knee tracks over your middle toe
note: With flat feet, single-leg landings show the ankle-knee collapse most clearly. Film one set from the front.

name: Hurdle Hops
doThisNotThat: Rebound over a row of low hurdles with short ground contacts. Don't use hurdles so tall you have to tuck and land heavy.
steps: Set 4-6 hurdles at 6-12 in, about 3 ft apart.
Two-foot jump over the first.
Rebound off the balls of the feet over each next one with minimal knee bend.
Land and walk back.
homeSwap: Hop over a rolled towel or shoes, line of 4.
note: Keep contacts low (30-50 per session total jumps) while your feet adapt.

name: Bounding
doThisNotThat: Exaggerated running strides for height and distance, hanging in the air. Don't do short choppy strides or reach the foot out in front.
steps: Jog in 3-4 steps.
Drive off one leg, knee of the other leg punching forward and up.
Land under the hips, mid-foot, and push into the next bound.
Use the opposite arm with each leg, big swings. Go 20-30 m.
homeSwap: Same drill on grass or a field.
note: Bounding is sprint and XC power in one drill: longer strides from the same effort.

name: A-Skip
doThisNotThat: A rhythmic skip with a high knee, toes up, and the foot striking down under the hip. Don't lean back or flop the foot down in front.
steps: Tall posture, slight forward lean.
Drive one knee up to hip height, toes pulled up.
Strike the foot down and back under the hip as the other knee rises.
Arms run opposite, elbows about 90°. Go 20 m.
homeSwap: Same drill in a hallway or the street.
note: Grooves the running pattern so the foot lands under you, cutting the overstriding that wastes energy in XC.

name: B-Skip
doThisNotThat: An A-skip plus a leg extension that paws back under the hip. Don't kick out straight-legged and land in front.
steps: Start as an A-skip.
At the top, extend the lower leg forward.
Claw it down and back so the foot lands under the hip.
Keep a steady rhythm. Go 20 m.
note: Trains the hamstrings at speed in the position where sprinters strain them.

name: Power Skip
doThisNotThat: Skip for maximum height with a big opposite arm drive. Don't do a lazy playground skip.
steps: Skip forward.
Drive off the ground with one leg, punching the other knee and the opposite arm up.
Go as high as possible, land and repeat the other side.
Go 20 m.
cues: Reach the sky with your knee
note: Teaches the arm and leg to fire together. You tend to fire the arm first, and here it has to sync with the leg drive.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Push hard enough that the hands leave the floor, then land with soft elbows. Don't do tiny hops with a sagging hip.
steps: High plank, hands just outside the shoulders, body in one line.
Lower for 1-2 s to 2 in off the floor.
Explode so the hands leave the floor.
Catch with bent elbows and reset.
homeSwap: Same drill; elevate the hands on a bed or couch edge to make it easier.
note: Upper-body rate of force development is what makes a jab snap. Stop when the hands stop leaving the floor.

name: Clap Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Get enough air to clap once and return the hands before landing. Don't clap if you can't keep the hips in line.
steps: High plank.
Lower fast to 2 in off the floor.
Explode up and clap once.
Catch with soft elbows and stay in a straight plank.
note: Only progress from plyo push-ups when every rep clears the floor by about 2 in.

name: Med-Ball Chest Pass
doThisNotThat: Throw the ball into a wall as hard as possible from a split stance, legs into hips into arms. Don't push it like a slow bench press.
steps: Stand 3-5 ft from a solid wall in a split stance, ball at the chest.
Shift weight back, then drive the back foot into the floor.
Punch the ball into the wall with both arms, finishing with arms straight.
Catch the rebound or let it drop, and reset.
homeSwap: Explosive push-up, or chest-throw a pillow or a basketball against the wall.
note: Ground force goes up through the legs to the arms. The back-foot drive trains the push that starts a cross.

name: Overhead Med-Ball Slam
doThisNotThat: Reach tall onto the toes, then slam down with your whole body, hips back. Don't just throw with the arms while standing tall.
steps: Feet hip-width, ball overhead, up on the toes, full stretch.
Snap the hips back and crunch down hard, driving the ball into the floor.
Throw it about 1 ft in front of the toes.
Pick it up and re-set to full height each rep.
cues: Smash a hole in the floor
homeSwap: Fast overhead pull-downs with a light dumbbell (no release), or slam a rolled towel.
note: A fun release for the nervous system, and it trains the lats-to-abs chain used in overhand rights and sprawls.

name: Rotational Med-Ball Slam
doThisNotThat: Pivot the feet and let the hips turn first, then slam the ball down outside the front foot. Don't rotate only the arms with the feet stuck.
steps: Stand square, ball overhead.
Pivot onto the back foot's toe as the hips turn.
Slam down outside the opposite foot.
Alternate sides.
homeSwap: Fast DB woodchop (no release) or a towel slam.
note: Builds the hips-before-arms order you are missing, with a target on the floor.

name: Med-Ball Scoop Toss
doThisNotThat: An underhand rotational throw from the back hip into a wall. Don't muscle it with the arms or stand square.
steps: Stand sideways 4-6 ft from a wall, athletic stance.
Load the ball on the back hip, weight on the back leg.
Drive the back foot and turn the hips toward the wall; the arms follow last.
Release low-to-high into the wall.
note: Same hip-first order as a forehand, a swing or a hook. Grade C: mechanism-based link to rotational sport power.

name: Med-Ball Side Toss
doThisNotThat: Throw from a shot-put position at chest height, back foot first. Don't push with the arm alone.
steps: Stand sideways to a wall, ball at the back shoulder.
Sit into the back hip.
Drive the back foot and rotate, finishing with the arm extending through the ball.
Catch and reset.
homeSwap: Rotational punch with a light dumbbell, held, not thrown.
note: The closest throw to a cross or a straight right: ground to hip to fist.

name: Overhead Backward Throw
doThisNotThat: Hinge down, then extend the hips violently and throw the ball back over your head. Don't pull with the arms and bend the back.
steps: Feet shoulder-width, ball at arm's length.
Hinge and squat to bring the ball between the knees.
Jump-extend the hips, knees and ankles and throw the ball up and back.
Do it in an open field, with no one behind you.
homeSwap: Max-height squat jump while swinging a light DB up (no release).
note: A whole-body triple-extension test. Distance tracks power, which makes it a good visible win.

name: Depth Push-Up
doThisNotThat: Drop the hands off low blocks to the floor and rebound instantly. Don't sink to the bottom and pause.
steps: Hands on two low blocks or books, plank position.
Pop the hands off the blocks to the floor.
Absorb briefly and explode back up onto the blocks.
Stay rigid from head to heels.
homeSwap: Use two thick books; same drill.
note: Advanced. Start only after 3x6 clean plyo push-ups.

name: Landmine Rotational Punch
doThisNotThat: Pivot the back foot and let the hip turn first, then punch the bar up and across. Don't press it with the arm from a square stance.
steps: Bar in the landmine, hold the end at the back shoulder with one hand, fighting stance.
Load the back hip.
Pivot the back foot (squash the bug) and drive the hip through.
Punch the bar up and forward until the arm is long, chin behind the shoulder.
Control it back to the shoulder.
homeSwap: DB rotational punch-throw with a light dumbbell.
note: The closest loaded copy of a cross. Your arm fires first, so start each rep with a 1 s back-foot pivot drill.

name: Cable Rotational Punch
doThisNotThat: Set the cable at shoulder height behind you and punch explosively from the hip. Don't use a weight so heavy that the turn slows down.
steps: Cable at shoulder height, handle in the rear hand, fighting stance facing away.
Load the back hip, hand at the chin.
Pivot the back foot, turn the hips, then extend the fist straight forward.
Return slowly to the guard.
homeSwap: Shadow cross with a 2-5 lb DB, held tight.
note: Light and fast: the goal is speed of rotation, not load.

name: Dumbbell Rotational Punch-Throw
doThisNotThat: Use a very light DB, rotate from the hip and punch, stopping the arm with control. Don't throw heavy weights with a locked elbow.
steps: Fighting stance, 2-5 lb DB at the chin.
Load the back leg.
Pivot, turn the hips, punch to full reach without locking the elbow.
Snap back to the guard.
note: Keep it 2-5 lb. Heavier slows the hand and grooves a pushing punch.

name: Hip Snap Drill
doThisNotThat: Turn the hips and pivot the back foot while the shoulders lag for a split second, then let them whip through. Don't turn everything as one block.
steps: Athletic stance, hands at the chest.
Load the back hip.
Snap the back hip forward and pivot the back heel out.
Feel the shoulders arrive a beat later.
Reset and repeat.
note: This is your core sequencing fix: hips lead, arm whips. Do it before swings, throws and punches.

name: Power Clean
doThisNotThat: Keep the bar close, extend the hips violently, then drop under fast into a quarter-squat catch. Don't pull early with the arms or reverse-curl it.
steps: Bar over mid-foot, shoulder-width grip, shins near the bar, chest up.
Push the floor away to lift the bar to the knees, back angle unchanged.
From mid-thigh, jump explosively: hips, knees, ankles extend, then shrug.
Pull yourself under, elbows whip around, catch on the shoulders in a quarter squat.
Stand up, return the bar under control.
cues: Jump the bar off your thighs
note: Learn it from a coach first. Technique decides how much power you get, and your arm-first habit shows up as an early arm pull.

name: Hang Clean
doThisNotThat: Start at mid-thigh, hinge, then jump and shrug. Don't bounce it off the thighs with a bent-arm pull.
steps: Stand with the bar at hip height.
Hinge with the bar sliding to just above the knees, shoulders over the bar.
Explode with the hips, shrug, then pull under.
Catch high in a quarter squat with the elbows forward.
note: Easier to learn than the full clean, and it teaches the hip snap that powers every jump.

name: Power Snatch
doThisNotThat: Wide grip, keep the bar close, extend explosively and punch up into a quarter squat overhead. Don't press it out at the top.
steps: Snatch-width grip (bar sits in the hip crease when standing).
Lift from the floor with the chest over the bar.
Jump from the hip crease, bar close.
Pull under and punch the arms straight overhead, catch in a quarter squat.
note: Requires overhead mobility that stiff shoulders may lack. Do wall slides and pass-throughs first, and use the DB version until the bar overhead feels easy.

name: Hang Snatch
doThisNotThat: Start from above the knee and snap the hips. Don't muscle-pull with bent arms.
steps: Snatch grip, bar at the hips.
Hinge to above the knee.
Explode, shrug, pull under.
Catch overhead in a quarter squat with arms locked.
note: Light only. It's a speed drill; a stiff thoracic spine pushes the bar forward.

name: Push Jerk
doThisNotThat: Dip and drive with the legs, then push yourself under the bar into a partial squat. Don't press it out with the arms.
steps: Bar in the front rack, feet hip-width.
Dip 3-4 in straight down, knees out.
Drive up hard and pop the bar off the shoulders.
Push yourself under and lock out in a quarter squat, then stand.
homeSwap: DB push press with light dumbbells.
note: A short, straight dip is a sharp, stiff stretch-shortening action, the same quality as a jump takeoff.

name: Split Jerk
doThisNotThat: Dip, drive, then split the feet front and back under the bar. Don't land with the feet in line or too narrow.
steps: Front rack.
Dip and drive.
Split one foot forward and one back, landing at the same time as the arms lock.
Recover the front foot back, then the back foot forward.
note: Coach-led only. Good for split-stance stability, which also carries over to fighting stance.

name: Clean Pull
doThisNotThat: Lift like a clean, extend hard onto the toes and shrug, with arms long. Don't bend the arms.
steps: Clean setup.
Lift to mid-thigh.
Explode upward: hips, knees, ankles, then shrug.
Lower under control.
note: Lets you train hip power heavier than you can catch, with no catch to learn yet.

name: High Pull
doThisNotThat: Jump first, then let the elbows ride high and out with the bar close. Don't do a slow upright-row grind.
steps: Hang position at mid-thigh.
Explode the hips.
Let the elbows rise high and out to bring the bar to the chest.
Control the bar down.
note: A safe way to learn the power transfer from hips to arms.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
doThisNotThat: Hinge, jump, and punch the DB overhead in one motion with the DB close. Don't curl or press it.
steps: DB between the feet, hinge, grab with one hand.
Drive the floor away and extend the hips hard.
Pull the DB close, elbow high, then punch it overhead as you dip.
Lock it out, then lower to the shoulder and back to the floor.
homeSwap: This is the home version: use your heaviest light DB for 5-8 per side.
note: Teaches whole-body power from the floor using only home dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Hang Clean
doThisNotThat: Hinge, jump, and catch the DBs on the shoulders. Don't curl them up.
steps: DBs at the sides.
Hinge with DBs to the knees.
Explode up and shrug, then pull under, catching on the shoulders.
Lower and repeat.
note: A cheap power drill for home. Stop when the catch gets sloppy.

name: Kettlebell Swing
doThisNotThat: A hip hinge with a violent hip snap that floats the bell to chest height. Don't squat it or lift it with the arms.
steps: Bell a foot in front. Hinge, grab, tilt it toward you.
Hike it back high between the thighs.
Snap the hips forward and squeeze the glutes; the bell floats to chest height.
Let it fall and hinge back late. Exhale hard at the top.
cues: Hike the bell like a football
homeSwap: Two-hand DB swing holding one end of a light DB.
note: A hinge for anyone stiff in the hamstrings. Also a 20-30 s conditioning interval, a good EIB warm-up item.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
doThisNotThat: One hand on the bell, square shoulders, and fight the twist. Don't let the shoulder get yanked forward.
steps: Same as a two-hand swing, one hand on the bell.
Free arm out to the side for balance.
Resist rotation as you swing.
Switch hands every set.
note: Adds anti-rotation for the core, the same demand as staying square while punching.

name: Kettlebell Clean
doThisNotThat: Hip snap, keep the bell close, and let it roll softly into the rack. Don't bang it on the forearm.
steps: Swing setup.
Hike back.
Snap the hips and pull the elbow back; the bell rolls around the hand into the rack.
Drop it back into the hike.
note: Teaches the tight hip-to-arm handoff that your sequencing lacks.

name: Acceleration Sprint
doThisNotThat: Lean forward from the ankles, push back with piston strides, and rise gradually over 10-20 yd. Don't pop upright on step 1 or reach the foot out front.
steps: Two-point stance, lean forward, opposite arm to the front leg.
Push the ground back and down with full extension.
Drive the knees, punch the arms cheek to hip.
Stay low for about 5 steps, rising over 10-20 yd.
Walk back and fully recover.
homeSwap: Treadmill sprints at 8-10% incline for 6-8 s, or hill sprints.
note: Do 8 x 30 s hard / 30 s easy first: the interval warm-up blunts EIB and its protective window lasts ~1-2 h. Measure your 10-yd time weekly; it's the purest speed number.

name: Flying Sprint
doThisNotThat: Build up for 20 m, then hit max speed for 10-20 m. Run tall and relaxed. Don't strain with a clenched face and shoulders.
steps: Mark a 20 m build zone and a 10-20 m fly zone.
Accelerate smoothly through the build zone.
Hit max speed in the fly zone, tall, with the foot landing under the hip.
Decelerate gradually, walk back.
cues: Hit the ground under your hips
homeSwap: Treadmill: hit max speed for 8-10 s, carefully; hold the rails to step off.
note: Relaxation is speed. Your threat state tenses you up, so practice loose shoulders and a soft jaw.

name: Hill Sprint
doThisNotThat: Sprint 8-10 s up a moderate hill driving the knees, then walk down. Don't run steep or long hills until you're cooked.
steps: Find a 5-10% hill.
Sprint up hard for 8-10 s with the hips tall.
Punch the arms, drive the knees, push the ground back.
Walk down for full recovery.
note: The incline caps top speed and shortens the stride, which makes hill sprints a safer way to build speed on the hamstrings. Do 8 x 30 s hard / 30 s easy first: the interval warm-up blunts EIB and its protective window lasts ~1-2 h.

name: Sled Push
doThisNotThat: Lean low with arms long and drive the ground back in short, powerful steps. Don't push upright with bent arms.
steps: Hands on the high poles, arms long, body at about 45°.
Drive one knee forward and push the ground back.
Short powerful steps, keep the hips low.
homeSwap: Treadmill push with the belt off (if safe), or a wall-drive march.
note: Pure acceleration mechanics with no eccentric soreness. Fine on game-week days.

name: Sled Pull
doThisNotThat: Walk backward with a long arm-line, the knee driving over the toe each step. Don't lean back and pull with the arms.
steps: Strap or rope to the sled.
Face the sled, sit into a quarter squat.
Step backward, pushing through the front of the foot.
Steady cadence for 20 m.
cues: Push the floor away with each step
homeSwap: Backward incline walk on the treadmill at low speed.
note: Builds knees and quads that stay healthy for jumping, and the reverse direction is easy on the joints.

name: 5-10-5 Pro Agility
doThisNotThat: Low hips, outside foot plants beyond your body, push off it. Don't round off the turn tall.
steps: Three cones 5 yd apart, start at the middle.
Sprint 5 yd right and touch the line.
Plant the outside foot, sink the hips, sprint 10 yd left and touch.
Sprint back 5 yd through the middle.
homeSwap: Same drill in a hallway or driveway.
note: The plant step is where the flat-foot cascade collapses the knee. Screw that foot in on every plant.

name: T-Drill
doThisNotThat: Sprint, then shuffle with no crossing feet, staying low. Don't turn the shoulders and run sideways.
steps: Cones in a T: 10 yd forward, 5 yd each side.
Sprint forward.
Shuffle left 5 yd, right 10 yd, left 5 yd.
Backpedal to start.
note: Teaches you to move the feet instead of reaching, the habit behind your random contact on the court.

name: L-Drill
doThisNotThat: Lean into each turn and keep the feet under the hips. Don't take wide, loopy turns.
steps: Three cones in an L, 5 yd apart.
Sprint to cone 2 and back.
Sprint around cone 2, weave around cone 3, and back.
Time it.
note: Tight turns need ankle control: a strong tripod foot keeps you from rolling out.

name: Agility Ladder Drills
doThisNotThat: Quick, light feet on the balls of the feet, eyes up. Don't stare at your feet or stomp flat-footed.
steps: Pick a pattern: one-in, two-in, ickey shuffle, in-out.
Start slow and perfect.
Speed up while staying rhythmic.
Finish with a 5 yd sprint out to tie it to real movement.
homeSwap: Draw a ladder with tape or chalk.
note: Ladders mostly train rhythm, not real game agility (grade C). Finish each rep with a sprint or a reaction to make it transfer.

name: Cone Drills
doThisNotThat: Cut at each cone with the outside foot plant and hips low. Don't round every cone tall.
steps: Set 4-6 cones in a zig-zag, 5 yd apart.
Sprint to each cone.
Plant the outside foot and cut hard to the next.
Accelerate out of each cut.
homeSwap: Same drill with shoes as markers.
note: Cutting is where ankles and knees get hurt. Own a slow, sticky cut before going fast.

name: Backpedal
doThisNotThat: Low hips, chest over the toes, quick reaching steps under you. Don't lean back and clomp on the heels.
steps: Athletic stance.
Push off the front of the feet, stepping back under the hips.
Arms run like a sprint.
Go 10-15 yd, then turn and sprint forward.
note: Football defense and boxing retreats depend on this.

name: Defensive Slides
doThisNotThat: Low hips, push off the trail leg and never click the heels together. Don't pop up tall or cross the feet.
steps: Ready position: knees ~25°, hip hinge ~15°.
Push off the trail foot, step the lead foot.
Keep a wide base, head level.
Slide 5-10 yd and back.
note: Hold your ready position for 60 s first so the angles are installed and you don't need to think about them in the game.

name: Shuttle Run
doThisNotThat: Sprint, touch, turn low, repeat with clean turns. Don't turn tall, flat-footed and sloppy.
steps: Lines at 5-25 yd.
Sprint to a line, touch with the outside hand.
Plant, sink, and turn back.
Repeat for the set distance.
note: Do 8 x 30 s hard / 30 s easy first: the interval warm-up blunts EIB and its protective window lasts ~1-2 h. Long shuttles are conditioning; keep HR rest-to-work honest.

name: Mirror Drill
doThisNotThat: React to a partner and stay square. Don't guess or cross your feet.
steps: Face your partner 3-5 ft apart, both in ready position.
Leader moves randomly: side, forward, back.
Follower mirrors with short steps, staying square.
10-15 s bursts, switch roles.
homeSwap: With your sibling: same drill, and they lead.
note: Pure reaction training against a live person, the best kind of reaction drill for your late reactions.

name: Reaction Ball Drill
doThisNotThat: Throw the ball against a wall and react to random bounces with your feet first, then your hand. Don't stand flat-footed and only reach.
steps: Stand 6-8 ft from a wall in ready position.
Throw the ball against the wall or the floor.
Move the feet to the bounce and catch.
Switch hands.
homeSwap: A tennis ball off the wall or a corner, or a partner drop drill.
note: Object approach without threat helps fear of the ball. Start close and slow, and add speed only when catching feels easy.

name: Treadmill Run
doThisNotThat: Run at a pace you can hold while breathing in a rhythm, cadence 170-180. Don't start every run at race pace.
steps: Set a 1% incline (matches outdoor effort).
Warm up: 5 min easy, then 4-6 x 20 s pickups.
Run at the target pace, cadence 170-180 (beat-synced music helps).
Cool down 3-5 min.
note: XC baseline ~8:22/mile at ~173 HR. Easy runs belong around 130-150 bpm, not 173. Pogos before runs tune the Achilles.

name: Zone 2 Run
doThisNotThat: Go slow enough to breathe through the nose, about 60-70% of max HR. Don't turn every easy run into a tempo.
steps: Pick a pace you can sustain with nasal breathing.
Walk breaks are allowed to stay in zone.
homeSwap: Treadmill incline walk at the same HR.
note: Your HR runs high naturally, so trust the nasal-breathing test over a strict number. Grade B-C for nasal breathing as a pacing tool.

name: Incline Walk
doThisNotThat: Walk at an incline without holding the rails. Don't hang on the handles.
steps: Incline 8-12%, speed 3-3.5 mph.
Walk tall, arms swinging.
Roll through each foot.
note: Low-impact Zone 2 when your legs are cooked or a game is close.

name: Treadmill Intervals
doThisNotThat: Hard repeats with set recovery, HR 85-95% of max. Don't go all-out on rep 1 and die by rep 4.
steps: Warm up 8 x 30 s hard / 30 s easy (EIB prep).
Main: e.g. 6-10 x 1 min hard (HR 172-190) / 1 min walk.
Keep every rep the same speed.
Cool down 5 min.
note: Do 8 x 30 s hard / 30 s easy first: the interval warm-up blunts EIB and its protective window lasts ~1-2 h. The aim is equal reps; if pace drops >5%, stop.

name: Norwegian 4x4
doThisNotThat: Four 4-min intervals at 85-95% of max HR with 3 min easy between. Don't start the first one at 100%.
steps: Warm up 10 min including 8 x 30 s pickups (EIB).
4 min at 85-95% max HR (~172-195 bpm); on a treadmill, use a 4-8% incline.
3 min active recovery at ~60-70% (walk or jog).
Repeat 4 times, then cool down.
cues: Smooth and strong, not a sprint
note: Once a week. HR lags, so rep 1 may only hit 85% by the end; that is normal.

name: Air Bike
doThisNotThat: Push and pull with arms and legs together for short all-out bursts. Don't hammer the legs only.
steps: Seat height: slight knee bend at the bottom.
Warm up 3-5 min easy.
Sprints: 10-20 s all-out, push-pull arms and legs.
Recover 40-60 s easy.
note: No impact, so it's great for conditioning on game-heavy weeks.

name: Stationary Bike
doThisNotThat: Use a seat height that gives a slight knee bend at the bottom, and a steady cadence of 80-100 rpm. Don't ride a seat that's too low with the knees jamming.
steps: Seat at hip height standing next to it.
Ball of the foot on the pedal.
Zone 2: steady and conversational for 30-45 min.
Or intervals: 30 s hard / 90 s easy.
note: Easy on the joints: use it for Zone 2 the day after a hard leg day.

name: Rowing Machine
doThisNotThat: Legs, then hips, then arms on the drive, and arms, hips, legs on the way back. Don't pull with the arms first.
steps: Strap the feet, damper 4-6.
Catch: shins vertical, arms long, chest tall.
Push the legs, then swing the hips back, then pull the handle to the ribs.
Return: arms, then hips, then knees. 1:2 drive-to-recovery rhythm.
cues: Push the floor away with the feet
note: Rowing exposes your arm-first habit. If the arms pull before the legs finish, slow down: the rower drills legs-then-body-then-arms.

name: Ski Erg
doThisNotThat: Hinge and crunch down with straight-ish arms, hips back. Don't pull with bent arms only.
steps: Stand close, arms up holding the handles.
Drive down with the lats and abs while hinging the hips back.
Finish with hands past the hips.
Stand tall and reach back up.
homeSwap: Overhead med-ball slam intervals with a towel, or burpees.
note: The same downward chain used in sprawls and overhand strikes.

name: Jump Rope
doThisNotThat: Small quiet jumps off the balls of the feet, wrists turn the rope. Don't do big jumps with arms swinging wide.
steps: Rope handles at armpit height when standing on the middle.
Elbows close to the ribs.
Turn the rope with the wrists.
Bounce 1-2 in off the floor.
homeSwap: Pogo hops in rhythm, or fake-rope (no rope) bounces.
note: Boxers use rope for rhythm and calf springiness. 3 x 3 min rounds with 1 min rest, like a fight.

name: Double-Unders
doThisNotThat: Jump a bit higher and spin the wrists twice as fast. Don't pike the legs or flail the arms.
steps: Get 30 smooth singles first.
Add one quick wrist flick per jump for two rotations.
Stay tall, legs nearly straight.
Build singles-double patterns.
note: A coordination win you can measure: count max unbroken doubles weekly.

name: Burpee
doThisNotThat: Hands down, jump back to a plank, chest down, jump up with clean form. Don't slap down like a worm with a sagging back.
steps: Squat, hands to the floor.
Jump the feet back to a plank.
Chest to the floor (optional), push up.
Jump the feet in and jump up with the hands overhead.
note: The burpee's jump-back is the same action as a sprawl, so you also get a combat drill.

name: Mountain Climbers
doThisNotThat: Hold a solid plank and drive the knees fast under the hips. Don't pike the butt up or bounce the hips.
steps: High plank, hands under the shoulders.
Drive one knee to the chest.
Switch fast, keeping the hips level.
Breathe rhythmically.
note: Good EIB-friendly interval item, since short bursts allow breathing control.

name: Stair Climber
doThisNotThat: Climb upright with the whole foot on each step, hands light on the rails. Don't lean on the rails at a hunch.
steps: Pick a speed you can keep without holding on.
Step through the whole foot.
Drive through the heel and mid-foot.
homeSwap: Walk or run your house stairs.
note: Good low-impact Zone 2 for XC season.

name: Battle Ropes
doThisNotThat: Athletic stance with fast waves powered by the hips and legs. Don't stand tall and only flick the arms.
steps: Quarter squat, rope ends in hands.
Make alternating or double waves.
Keep the waves reaching the anchor.
20-30 s bursts.
homeSwap: Fast DB shadowboxing with 1-2 lb, or a towel snap drill.
note: Builds shoulder endurance for keeping your guard up in round 3.

name: Bear Crawl
doThisNotThat: Knees 1 in off the floor, back flat, opposite hand and foot move together. Don't crawl with the butt high.
steps: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, lift the knees 1 in.
Move opposite hand and foot together in small steps.
Keep the back flat and the hips still.
Crawl forward, backward, sideways.
note: Contralateral crawling patterns help the coordination behind your wobbly walk. Grade C, mechanism-based.

name: Swimming
doThisNotThat: Long, relaxed strokes with steady exhales underwater. Don't hold your breath and thrash.
steps: Warm up 2-4 easy lengths.
Swim steady laps, exhaling through the nose underwater.
Rest at the wall as needed.
note: Warm humid air is easier on EIB for many asthmatics. Never do breath-hold work in water.

name: Elliptical
doThisNotThat: Upright with full strides and steady cadence. Don't lean on the handles.
steps: Stand tall.
Push and pull the handles in rhythm.
Full stride.
note: A low-impact Zone 2 option when your shins are beat.

name: Shadowboxing Rounds
doThisNotThat: Throw every punch with the hips leading and the hand returning to the guard, moving your feet. Don't stand still flinging arms.
steps: Fighting stance: lead foot slightly turned in, back heel up, chin down, hands at the cheekbones.
Round 1: footwork + jab only.
Round 2: 1-2, 1-2-3, with a slip or pivot after each combo.
Round 3: free, at 70% effort, visualizing an opponent.
homeSwap: This is the home version: use a mirror.
note: Contact ladder level 0, so it's always safe with your sibling around. Zahabi: 70% effort, often, beats rare max sessions.

name: Heavy Bag Rounds
doThisNotThat: Strike through a spot 3 in inside the bag, turning the hips, and move after each combo. Don't push the bag or stand flat-footed in front of it.
steps: Wrap your hands, put on gloves.
Stand at jab distance.
Work in 2-3 min rounds: combo, angle out, reset.
Focus on snap and return, not arm power.
homeSwap: Shadowboxing Rounds with 1-2 lb dumbbells, or a pillow on the wall for alignment.
note: Wrap your hands every time; bones in a teenager's hand are still growing. Keep the bag at 70-80% power most rounds.

name: Double-End Bag
doThisNotThat: Light, accurate shots, then slip or reset as the ball rebounds. Don't swing hard and get tagged on the rebound.
steps: Stand at jab range.
Jab and watch the rebound.
Add slips and counters off the return.
2 min rounds.
homeSwap: Reaction ball drills or a tennis ball on a string.
note: An excellent rebound target for training your eyes: object approach that's safe and predictable, which helps the fear-of-ball freeze.

name: Speed Bag
doThisNotThat: Small circles with the side of the fist, steady rhythm. Don't punch it straight on, hard.
steps: Bag at mouth level.
Hit with the side of the fist in small circles.
Let it rebound 3 times (front-back-front), then hit again.
Switch hands in rhythm.
homeSwap: Fist rolls in front of a mirror, or wall-ball juggling.
note: Mostly a rhythm and shoulder-endurance drill; low transfer to real punching power. Grade C.

name: Focus Mitts
doThisNotThat: Partner calls the combos, you hit the pad with snap and return. Don't follow the pad and drop your guard.
steps: Partner holds the mitts at face height and calls numbers.
Throw the called combo, then return to the guard.
Add defense: the partner swats back and you slip or block.
2-3 min rounds.
homeSwap: Shadowboxing Rounds with a partner calling combos.
note: Contact ladder level 1: fine with your sibling holding pads. Keep their hands safe with light, accurate shots.

name: Slip Drills
doThisNotThat: Bend the knees and turn the shoulders a few inches to slip, eyes up. Don't bend at the waist or look at the floor.
steps: String a rope at chin height.
Walk under it with small bob and weaves, knees bending.
Slip left and right by turning the shoulders, not leaning.
Throw a counter after each slip.
homeSwap: A broom handle on two chairs, or a string across a doorway.
note: Head movement that is installed, not thought, kills the freeze response. Daily rounds at level 0.

name: Boxing Footwork Drills
doThisNotThat: The foot nearest the direction moves first and the other follows, keeping stance width. Don't cross the feet or bounce high.
steps: Fighting stance.
Step forward: front foot first, back foot follows.
Step back: back foot first. Same for sides.
Add pivots off the lead foot: 90° turns.
homeSwap: Same drill, with tape marks on the floor.
note: Footwork is the base for moving your feet instead of reaching. Tripod foot through every step.

name: Sprawl
doThisNotThat: Shoot the legs back and drop the hips onto the floor (onto the opponent), then pop back up. Don't land on your knees or with your hips high.
steps: Fighting stance.
Explosively kick both legs back, hips dropping to the floor.
Hands catch the floor, chest heavy, head up.
Snap back to the stance.
note: Contact ladder level 0, so it's safe solo. Also great conditioning: 30 s of sprawls is brutal.

name: Double-Leg Shot
doThisNotThat: Change levels first, step deep between their feet, drive with the head up and the back straight. Don't dive in head down from too far away.
steps: Stance, level change: bend the knees, not the waist.
Penetration step: lead knee drops to the mat between their feet.
Head on their chest/side, arms wrap the back of the thighs.
Drive off the back foot, turn the corner.
Solo: shoot across the mat and stand back up.
homeSwap: Solo penetration steps across the room.
note: Contact ladder level 2 at most with your sibling: cooperative drilling, they let you finish. Mat or soft floor only.

name: Single-Leg Shot
doThisNotThat: Change levels, attack the lead leg, secure it high and finish by running the pipe or driving. Don't reach for the leg from far away.
steps: Level change.
Step to the outside of the lead foot.
Grab behind the knee, pull the leg to your hip.
Head inside, finish by driving or turning.
homeSwap: Solo level changes and penetration steps.
note: Level 2 drilling only with your sibling. Tap early, light pressure.

name: Hip Escape
doThisNotThat: Bridge onto your shoulder, push the floor away with your foot and slide the hips back. Don't just slide flat on your back.
steps: On your back, knees bent.
Turn to one side onto the shoulder.
Push the floor away with the bottom foot and shoot the hips back.
Hands frame as if pushing a hip away. Travel the mat.
cues: Push the floor away with the foot
note: The BJJ fundamental. Level 0 solo, daily 2-3 lengths of the room.

name: Bridge and Roll
doThisNotThat: Trap one side (arm and foot), then bridge high and over the shoulder on that side. Don't bridge straight up.
steps: On your back, partner (or imagined) in mount.
Trap their arm to your chest and their foot with your foot on the same side.
Bridge hard over the shoulder on the trapped side.
Roll into their guard.
note: Level 2 with your sibling: they go limp, let you roll. Glute bridge strength makes it powerful.

name: Technical Stand-Up
doThisNotThat: Base on a hand and foot, lift the hips and swing the leg behind you into stance, hands up. Don't stand up forward with your face exposed.
steps: Sit, one hand posted behind, the opposite foot planted.
Other hand up as a frame.
Lift the hips, swing the free leg back through.
Land in fighting stance.
note: Teaches getting up safely, from fights and from falls on any field.

name: Sit-Out
doThisNotThat: From all fours, kick one leg through and turn to face the other way, hips low. Don't sit straight back on your butt.
steps: On all fours.
Kick the leg through under the body.
Turn the hips so you face the other way, sitting low.
Return and alternate.
note: Builds hip rotation for your stiff hips under load, plus a bottom-position escape.

name: Granby Roll
doThisNotThat: Roll over the shoulders, not the neck, with the head tucked to the side. Don't roll on top of your head.
steps: From a kneeling base, tuck one shoulder.
Roll across the shoulders with feet walking.
Keep the weight on the shoulders.
Come up to base or turn into the opponent.
homeSwap: Practice on a soft mattress first.
note: Learn from a coach. With stiff necks and backs, start with shoulder rolls first.

name: Level Change Drill
doThisNotThat: Bend the knees to drop straight down with the back straight and eyes up. Don't bend at the waist and look at the floor.
steps: Fighting stance.
Drop 6-12 in by bending the knees, hands up.
Pop back up.
Add a feint jab before each drop.
note: Head up and spine stacked protects the neck. Level 0, daily.

name: Clinch Knee Drill
doThisNotThat: Pull the head or bag down, drive the hips forward and the knee up. Don't lean back with just the leg.
steps: Hold a bag or imagined head with both hands.
Step back with the striking leg.
Drive the hips forward and knee up.
Alternate.
cues: Pull down as the knee goes up
homeSwap: Air knees at a wall, holding the top of a door frame for support.
note: Hips lead again. Light on a partner: level 2 max.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
doThisNotThat: Sit tall and rotate the knees side to side with the hands off the floor if you can. Don't slump with the hands propping you up.
steps: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one in front, one to the side.
Sit tall.
Rotate both knees to the other side.
Move slowly, pausing at the end range.
note: Your hips are stiff in rotation, which robs punching and swinging. Do this daily in your Morning 5.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Couch Stretch
doThisNotThat: Back knee at the wall, squeeze the glute, tuck the pelvis. Don't arch the lower back to fake range.
steps: Kneel with the back shin up a wall or couch.
Front foot forward in a lunge.
Squeeze the glute on the back leg, tuck the pelvis.
Stay tall and breathe 60 s.
note: Tight hip flexors reduce hip extension for sprinting. Do this after training, not before power work.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: World's Greatest Stretch
doThisNotThat: Lunge, drop the elbow to the instep, rotate the arm to the sky, then shift back into a hamstring stretch. Don't rush through it.
steps: Big lunge, back knee off the floor.
Same-side elbow down to the instep.
Rotate that arm up to the ceiling, eyes follow.
Hands down, shift hips back to straighten the front leg.
note: A full-body warm-up in one move for all-over stiffness.

name: Deep Squat Hold
doThisNotThat: Sit in a deep squat, heels down and chest up, with knees out. Don't let the heels lift and the feet collapse.
steps: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit all the way down.
Elbows push the knees out.
Hold a doorframe if needed; breathe 30-60 s.
note: Flat feet collapse here: keep the tripod and screw the feet. Elevate the heels on a book if needed at first.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Hip CARs
doThisNotThat: Draw the biggest slow circle with the knee while the rest of the body stays still. Don't swing fast.
steps: Stand holding a wall.
Lift the knee, open it out, rotate back and down, slowly.
Keep the pelvis still.
Reverse direction.
note: Controlled range is range the nervous system will let you use. Grade C.

name: Shoulder CARs
doThisNotThat: Slow, biggest-possible arm circles with the ribs still. Don't swing.
steps: Stand tall, make a fist.
Raise the arm forward and overhead, then rotate it back and down.
Keep the ribs down.
Reverse.
note: For a stiff upper back and shoulders before pressing and boxing.

name: Open Book Rotation
doThisNotThat: Lie on your side with the knees stacked and open the top arm to the floor behind, eyes following. Don't let the knees come apart.
steps: Lie on your side, knees bent to 90°, arms straight forward.
Open the top arm in an arc to the other side.
Eyes follow, exhale.
Return.
note: Upper-back rotation is the link that lets the hips hand off to the arm.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rocks
doThisNotThat: Knee travels over the pinky toe with the heel down and the arch up. Don't let the arch collapse to fake range.
steps: Half-kneel facing a wall.
Front foot about 4 in from the wall.
Drive the knee forward toward the wall, heel down.
Hold 2 s, rock back.
note: Flat feet fake ankle range by collapsing the arch. Keeping the arch lifted during this is the real fix.

name: Calf and Soleus Stretch
doThisNotThat: Straight knee for the calf, bent knee for the soleus, heel on the floor. Don't roll onto the inside of the foot.
steps: Hands on a wall, one leg back.
Back heel down, knee straight, 30 s.
Bend the back knee, 30 s.
Keep the arch lifted.
note: After runs, not before. Keeps the spring flexible for XC.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Pigeon Stretch
doThisNotThat: Front shin across, hips square, fold slowly over the front shin. Don't twist or let the knee hurt.
steps: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind the wrist, shin angled across.
Slide the back leg straight back.
Square the hips, fold over the front leg.
Breathe 60 s.
note: Any knee pain = swap to a figure-4 stretch on your back.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Frog Stretch
doThisNotThat: Knees wide, rock the hips back slowly. Don't bounce.
steps: On all fours, slide the knees wide.
Shins parallel, feet in line with knees.
Rock the hips back slowly.
Breathe.
note: Adductor range protects the groin in cutting and wrestling; pair with Copenhagen strength.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Hamstring Nerve Floss
doThisNotThat: Seated, extend the knee while looking up, then bend it while looking down. Don't hold a hard static stretch.
steps: Sit on a chair, slight slump.
Straighten one knee as you look up.
Bend the knee as you look down.
Smooth and easy, 10-15 reps.
note: Much of your "tight hamstring" feeling can be a protective nerve. Sliders calm it down. Grade C.

name: Cat-Cow
doThisNotThat: Move one vertebra at a time in rhythm with the breath. Don't snap through it.
steps: All fours.
Inhale: drop the belly, lift the chest (cow).
Exhale: round the back, tuck the chin (cat).
Slow, 8-10 reps.
note: A gentle downshift for a stiff spine; good in nightly mobility.

name: Wall Slides
doThisNotThat: Back and arms against the wall, slide up keeping the ribs down. Don't arch the lower back.
steps: Stand with the back to the wall, feet 6 in out.
Arms in a W against the wall.
Slide up to a Y without losing contact.
Ribs down.
note: Prerequisite for safe overhead pressing and snatching with stiff shoulders.

name: Stick Pass-Through
doThisNotThat: Wide grip, straight arms, slowly over and behind. Don't go narrow and force it.
steps: Hold a broomstick very wide.
Lift it overhead with straight arms.
Continue behind to the lower back.
Bring it back. Narrow the grip slowly over weeks.
note: Builds the overhead range boxing and snatching need. Never force pain.

name: Short-Foot Exercise
doThisNotThat: Pull the ball of the foot toward the heel to lift the arch without curling the toes. Don't crunch the toes.
steps: Sit, foot flat.
Without curling the toes, slide the ball toward the heel.
Arch lifts; hold 5 s.
Progress to standing, then single-leg.
cues: Make a dome under your foot
note: Meta-analysis shows a small effect on navicular drop; the real win is control (grade B-C).

name: Toe Yoga
doThisNotThat: Lift the big toe with the others down, then switch. Don't let the foot roll.
steps: Sit or stand barefoot.
Lift the big toe; keep the others down.
Then press the big toe down and lift the other four.
Alternate slowly.
note: Independent toe control is what the tripod foot needs.

name: Hip Distraction Stretch
doThisNotThat: Band pulls the hip joint gently while you sink into the stretch. Don't pinch the front of the hip.
steps: Band around the upper thigh, anchored behind.
Step into a lunge or kneeling stretch.
Let the band pull the hip back.
Hold 60 s.
homeSwap: No band: a half-kneeling hip flexor rock-and-hold, or a deep squat hold.
note: Grade C. Often feels better than a normal stretch if your hip pinches.

prescription.reps: 30-60 s or 5-8 slow reps per side

name: Foam Rolling
doThisNotThat: Roll slowly with breathing, spending 30-60 s per area. Don't grind on painful spots or roll the lower back.
steps: Roller under the target muscle.
Roll slowly 2-3 in at a time.
Breathe out on tender spots.
30-60 s per area.
homeSwap: A rolling pin, or a tennis ball against a wall.
note: Short-term range and comfort only (grade B-C). It's a downshift tool, not a fix.
